en: The Sūtra on the Great Universal Samantabhadra Dhāraṇī, translated by an unknown master, now appended to the Liang dynasty records.
Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda:
"I shall now proclaim the Great Samantabhadra Dhāraṇī;
you should receive and uphold it."
Tadhe tadhe | Aṭa naṭa | Camicaca | Cakuli kulica ya | Kulica yavati | Sthiti sthita | Vamoti ānanda | This is the Great Universal Benevolence Spell (Mahā-Samantabhadra-dhāraṇī).
It wards off and extinguishes all weapons;
it eliminates all enemies and adversaries;
and it removes all fears of yakṣas, rākṣasas, and other such beings.
Excluding all those named among the lower ghosts who are not permitted to eat:
Humadhu (1) Oṣahūhū Humadhu (2) Anukarpi Humadhu (3) Parāhumadhu (4) Svāhā (5).
Chant the mantra over water seven times and have the patient drink it.
For pains in the waist and legs, the names of the demons are: 1. Huluduo-yipozhala; 2. Huludou; 3. Bimoluo-huludou; 4. Miliqili-bei-huludou; 5. Svāhā.
Take three-colored threads— blue, yellow, and green—
and tie them into seven knots.
Fasten them around the ankles, then around the thighs, and finally around the waist.
The names of the headache-demons are: 1. Humadumakaghaṭāla, 2. Vimaghāṭāla, 3. Huhurakaghaṭāla, 4. Ihukaghaṭāla, 5. Imikajñighaṭāla, 6. Svāhā.
Recite the mantra seven times over willow twigs and strike [the patient] fourteen times.
The names of the dull-witted spirits are: (1) Bhūta-bhūta, (2) Phulla-phulla, (3) Añjana-huṭṭa, (4) Phulla-añjana-huṭṭa, (5) Ehu-parañjana-huṭṭa, (6) Śrīmukhi-ehu-parañjana, (7) Svāhā.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times for seven days, three times each day.
For earache, the name of the spirit is: 1. Bini-pa-ā-ti-ṭhi; 2. Vi-ni-pa-hu-ṇi-ṭhi; 3. Vi-ni-pa-i-hu-ṭhi; 4. Ni-ṭhi-pa-i-hu-ṭhi; 5. Ki-ma-ni-vi-ni-pa; 6. Svāhā.
On the first day of the moon’s appearance,
if the left ear aches, one should sit facing south;
if the right ear aches, one should sit facing north.
The door faces east; the patient sits inside the door and the incantation master sits outside the door.
The water is also placed outside the door; one sprinkles it twenty-one times, three times over.
The names of the demons of urinary obstruction (*mūtragraha*) are: (1) *Pabara*, (2) *Iphuri phuri pabara*, (3) *Cemuna pabara*, and (4) *Huhura capara*.
Fever diseases, illnesses caused by spirits and deities,
sorcery, malevolent poisons, incantations,
and the *vitarda-pautana* and other such [rites].
Wherever good sons or good daughters go—
whether on a path, across water, or in a place of urgent peril— they should recollect this mantra.
There will be no fear of yakṣas, nor of piśācas, kūṣmāṇḍas, kaṭapūtanas, rākṣasas, vaitālās, and the like.
Furthermore, there shall be no fear of water, fire, swords, staves, weapons, calamities, poisons, spells, incantations, or any such evils caused by humans or non-humans.
Ānanda, should there be any terror or urgent distress, [one should recite this].
One should recite and keep this mantra in mind;
none shall be able to cause harm or affliction.
Furthermore, Ānanda, if there are those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this mantra, [they shall be protected].
Just as the gods, nāgas, spirits, the twenty-eight divisions of humans and non-humans,
and others are unable to transgress or violate this mantra,
so too shall the iron wheel and the vajra wheel inflict suffering and affliction upon them.
May their heads be split into seven pieces—
four in the cardinal directions, four in the intermediate directions,
and one above and one below— for anyone who conceives an evil mind toward this person.
They shall all bind their poisonous minds so that they do not arise.
These sons and daughters of good family should skillfully read, recite, uphold, and practice [this].
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Great Samantabhadra Dhāraṇī
